title: Evangelion: the Gospel cycle after Pentecost, and the eothina
scope: The Gospel of every day from the Tuesday after Pentecost to the Saturday before the Publican and the Pharisee, in two series: Matthew (week N ends with the Nth Sunday after Pentecost) and Luke (counted from the Lukan jump). Also the eleven Resurrection Gospels of Sunday Matins (series 'eothina', week = number).
licence: Released with bible-rs under the MIT licence. The table holds Scripture references only: no Bible text and no prose from the sources. Notes are our own.
usage: Byzantine usage, Revised Julian fixed feasts, Julian Paschalion, in two usages: Greek (the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America as goarch.org prints it; the default) and Antiochian (the Antiochian Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America's service texts and charts). Where they differ both are recorded: a reading or an entry marked "in": "greek" or "antiochian" is read only in that usage, and an entry's "greek" or "antiochian" object changes its name, its rules (weekday, sunday, saturday, bright; none = no reading) or its confidence there. Slavic (OCA) and other alternatives (a patron's readings) are kept in 'variants' and 'slavic' and are never read.
numbering: English Bible (KJV/Hebrew) chapter and verse, the grid's numbering, with half-verse letters dropped. Each string in refs is one contiguous range ('Book C:V', 'Book C:V-V' or 'Book C:V-C:V', with the grid's book abbreviations); a reading's refs are read together, in order, as one lesson.
confidence: high: a source of the usage (the Antiochian service texts and charts; goarch.org) agrees with at least one independent source. medium: the sources differ (usually by a verse at the start or end) or the reference rests on one source. low: no Antiochian or Greek source was found, or the yearly ordo decides.

rules: Matthew is read from Pentecost to the Sunday after the Elevation (the first Sunday after 14 September). The Monday after it starts Luke week 1, however many Matthew weeks were read (the Lukan jump). Only the Gospel jumps.

On the Old calendar the Elevation comes 13 days later, so the 18th and 19th weeks after Pentecost can come before the jump. The table reads Luke weeks 1 and 2 there, as orthocal.info's computed Greek table does and as the Slavic books number them, and Luke week 1 starts again after the jump. No Greek source gives a rule for these weeks (Scrivener's Synaxarion has none), so they are low confidence.
Luke weekdays count forward from the jump until the Nativity, and backward from the Triodion after Theophany: the last week before the Publican reads week 16, the one before week 15, then 14.

Luke Sundays from September to December: the Sunday 11-17 October reads the 4th, 30 October-5 November the 5th, 24-30 November the 13th, 1-3 December the 14th, 4-10 December the 10th, 11-17 December the 11th; other Sundays take 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 in order.

Sundays from Theophany to the Triodion: with n Sundays from the Sunday after Theophany to the Publican, the middle n-2 take the first n-2 of 12th, 15th and 14th of Luke, 16th and 15th of Matthew not read in the autumn (Luke first, ascending, then Matthew); the last is the Canaanite Woman (17th of Matthew) when n >= 4, otherwise Zacchaeus (15th of Luke). The Archdiocese's charts differ on leaving out a Gospel read in the autumn: in 2019 the chart left out the 14th of Luke, read on 2 December 2018, as goarch.org does every winter; in 2024 it read the 14th again although it had been read on 3 December 2023. The table follows 2019 and goarch.org.
Eothina: Sunday N after Pentecost (All Saints = 1) reads eothinon ((N - 1) mod 11) + 1, through the 5th Sunday of Lent.

entries.name: Monday of the 17th week after Pentecost
entries.note: Matthew week 17 weekdays occur in place only when Pascha falls on or before April 6 (2010, 2037, 2048 in 1990-2099), because the Lukan jump comes first. Scrivener's Byzantine Synaxarion has no weekday lessons for this week. The reference given is the Slavic/OCA assignment (the same Mark pericopes as Luke week 15). antiochian.org used different readings under '17TH ... AFTER PENTECOST' labels in a winter surplus week (2019-02-04 Mark 5:24-34, 2019-02-05 Mark 6:1-7, 2019-02-07 Mark 6:30-45, i.e. the Matthew week 15 pericopes), while goarch.org read Luke week 15 on those days. Treat as unresolved for Antiochian usage.

entries.name: 17th Sunday of Matthew (The Canaanite woman)
entries.note: Sunday of the Canaanite Woman. Almost never read in September in Greek usage (only when Pascha is on or before April 6). In Greek/Antiochian usage it is read on the last Sunday before the Publican and Pharisee when there are four or more Sundays from the Sunday after Theophany to the Triodion (antiochian.org 2019-02-10, 2021-02-14, 2022-02-06, 2023-01-29, 2024-02-18). Wikipedia's Paschal-cycle article names the 11th Sunday before Pascha 'Sunday of the Canaanite' in Greek usage and 'Zacchaeus Sunday' in Slavic usage. Scrivener's medieval Synaxarion also lists it as a 17th Sunday of Luke.

entries.name: 14th Sunday of Luke (The blind man near Jericho)
entries.note: Fixed to a Sunday Dec 1-3 when there is one (years whose Sunday after the Elevation is Sept 15-17). Otherwise it is read after Theophany when the winter is long enough (antiochian.org 2021-01-24, 2022-01-23; in 2024 antiochian.org read it after Theophany as well although it had been read on 2023-12-03).

entries.name: 15th Sunday of Luke (Zacchaeus)
entries.note: Zacchaeus. Read after Theophany. It is the last Sunday before the Triodion only when there are three or fewer Sundays from the Sunday after Theophany to the Triodion (antiochian.org 2018-01-21, 2026-01-25); in longer winters the Canaanite Woman follows it. Slavic/OCA always puts Zacchaeus on the Sunday before the Publican and Pharisee.
